Start here

What GallerySync is for, what it promises, and how the app is laid out.

What GallerySync is, and what it is not

GallerySync keeps your photos and videos safe in your Cloud and helps you control how much room they take on your phone.

It is not a gallery app. Viewing, searching, editing and sharing stay in the gallery app you already use.

What it does

  • Backup: copies your photos and videos to your Cloud.
  • Optimise: once a file is safely in the Cloud, swaps the phone's copy for a smaller one. It stays in your gallery.
  • Archive: once an album is safely in the Cloud, moves the phone's copies to the phone's trash to free space.
  • Restore: brings full-size files back from the Cloud.

What it does not do

There are no GallerySync servers. Your files go straight between your phone and your own Cloud account.

The safety promises
  • Nothing is permanently deleted. Anything removed goes to a trash or recycle bin you can recover from.
  • The app never empties a bin. Only you do that.
  • Nothing leaves your phone unless you chose Archive for that album, and you confirm that choice.
  • "Safe" means verified. The Cloud must confirm it holds the file at the same file size before anything is optimised or removed.
  • Out of the box, nothing happens. No folders are chosen and every album is Off until you decide.
  • Your Cloud copies are left alone. By default, deleting a photo on your phone does not touch its Cloud copy. Choose Ask me about the Cloud copy in Settings to be offered the choice; nothing is removed unless you select it and confirm.

Good to know

Now and then, open your Cloud and look at a few photos, especially before you empty a bin.

The Four Tabs Menu

The bar at the bottom has four tabs. The tab you are on shows its name.

  • Albums (folder): set each album's mode and run backups.
  • Restore (cloud with arrow): bring files back from your Cloud.
  • Archive (cloud with check mark): check Archive albums and remove them from the phone.
  • Settings (cog): Clouds, folders, optimising and other preferences.

Tap any (?) for a short explanation. The full guide is the first card in Settings.

Quick start
  1. Finish setup: sign in to your Cloud, allow access to your photos, choose folders and a Backup Plan. See “How the setup works”.
  2. On the Albums tab, tap an album's mode button and choose Backup.
  3. New photos are backed up automatically. Press Sync now to back up straight away.
  4. Check each album's last line: it shows how many files your Cloud has confirmed.
  5. Need space? Choose Sync to optimise an album, or Archive to move it off the phone.
  6. Need a file back at full size? Use the Restore tab.
Words you will see
  • Album: a folder of photos and videos on your phone.
  • Mode: what happens to an album: Off, Backup, Sync or Archive. See “The four modes”.
  • Cloud: OneDrive, Google Photos, Google Drive, Dropbox, pCloud, IDrive e2 or Backblaze B2. See “Cloud storage: choosing services, signing in and choosing where backups go”.
  • Pairing: which Cloud each top-level folder on your phone sends to. DCIM, Pictures and the other folders your phone keeps photos in are what the Guide calls top-level folders. See “Where each folder goes”.
  • Optimise: replace the phone's copy with a smaller one; the original stays in the Cloud. See “How optimising works”.
  • Verified: the Cloud confirmed it holds the file at the same size. See “How verification works”.
  • Trash / Recycle Bin: where removed files wait. See “Where removed files go”.
  • Rescan: look at the phone and the Cloud again for fresh numbers.

First-time setup

A guided setup runs the first time you open GallerySync.

How the setup works

Next moves on, Back goes back. A screen lets you continue only when it has what it needs.

The steps

  1. Welcome, a short tour, and what will be set up. See “Welcome, the tour, and what will be set up”.
  2. Choose your Clouds and sign in. See “Cloud storage: choosing services, signing in and choosing where backups go”.
  3. Allow access to your photos, then choose folders. See “Choose folders to back up”.
  4. Choose a Backup Plan.
  5. Optimisation settings (plans 2 and 3 only).
  6. When to start.
  7. The first backup: check the Cloud, upload, then optimise if your plan includes it.

Good to know

  • The first backup can take hours. It carries on if you leave the app.
  • The app opens on the progress screen until the first backup is finished.
  • Setup answers apply to the first backup only. See “Setup and Settings are separate”.
Welcome, the tour, and what will be set up
  • Welcome: choose your language to continue. You can change it later in Settings.
  • The tour: five screens, one for each tab and one for Help.
  • What we'll set up: sign in to your Cloud, allow photo access, choose folders, and allow changes to those folders.

The link at the bottom of that screen opens this setup guide. It is the only part of the guide available during setup.

Cloud storage: choosing services, signing in and choosing where backups go

Select the Clouds you use and press Next. Nothing is selected to start with.

Your first Cloud is free

The first Cloud you select becomes your free Cloud, shown as main (free) in Settings. Each further Cloud needs Pro: free for 30 days, then a one-time purchase. Nothing is charged automatically. If the trial ends, extra Clouds pause and your free Cloud carries on.

Start the trial with Start 30-day free trial in Settings, under Backup; it appears once a second Cloud is connected. Unlock Pro buys it.

What each Cloud can do

  • OneDrive, Google Drive, Dropbox, pCloud, IDrive e2 and Backblaze B2: Backup, Sync, Archive and Restore.
  • Google Photos: backup only.

A note about duplicates

OneDrive is the only Cloud whose contents are checked before anything is sent. Other Clouds may receive a second copy of a file that is already there.

Signing in

Each Cloud gets its own numbered Connect card. Next waits until all are connected.

  • OneDrive, Google Photos, Google Drive, Dropbox, pCloud: sign in on the provider's own page. Your password never goes into GallerySync. For Dropbox, allow read and write, or Restore will not work.
  • IDrive e2, Backblaze B2: enter the keys from their console. See “Connecting Backblaze B2: the keys and where to find them” and “Connecting IDrive e2: the keys and where to find them”.

Backup folder

Once a Cloud is connected, its card shows its Backup folder, with Change to pick another (not Google Photos, which has no folders). OneDrive starts at Samsung Gallery / DCIM, the folder Samsung's own OneDrive sync uses, so photos already synced there are not sent twice. Other Clouds start at GallerySync. See “Where new backups go (the Change dialog)”.

Connecting Backblaze B2: the keys and where to find them

GallerySync only writes inside its backup folder in your bucket (GallerySync unless you choose another), so an existing bucket is safe to use.

In Backblaze

  1. A private bucket: use one you have, or Buckets → Create a Bucket.
  2. Its endpoint: shown in the bucket's details, for example s3.us-east-005.backblazeb2.com.
  3. An application key: Application Keys → Add a New Application Key, for that one bucket, Read and Write. Not the Master key.
  4. Copy both halves: the keyID and the applicationKey. The applicationKey is shown only once.

In GallerySync

  • Endpoint: without https://.
  • Region: leave blank.
  • Bucket name: exactly as in Backblaze.
  • Access key ID: the keyID (starts with 005).
  • Secret access key: the applicationKey. Tap Show to check it.

If the keys are rejected

The message says what to check. It is nearly always a typo: O vs zero, I vs l, J vs j. Pasting avoids this.

Connecting IDrive e2: the keys and where to find them

GallerySync only writes inside its backup folder in your bucket (GallerySync unless you choose another), so an existing bucket is safe to use.

In IDrive e2

  1. A private bucket.
  2. The region's endpoint, for example s3.us-west-1.idrivee2.com. Not the address with the bucket name in front.
  3. The region name, for example us-west-1.
  4. An access key: an access key ID and secret access key. The secret is shown only once.

In GallerySync

Enter the Endpoint (without https://), Region, Bucket name, Access key ID and Secret access key. Tap Show to check the secret.

If the keys are rejected

The message says what to check. It is nearly always a typo: O vs zero, I vs l. Pasting avoids this.

Let GallerySync search this phone

Give search permission opens Android's permission screen. This is where you let GallerySync see the photos and videos on your phone.

Good to know

Choose Allow all. If you choose Select photos, only those photos can be backed up.

Choose folders to back up

Select the folders to back up and press Next. Most photos are in DCIM.

Which Cloud each folder goes to

With more than one Cloud, each folder shows Goes to. Choose a Cloud for every selected folder. Files already sent never move; only new files follow a change. See “Where each folder goes”.

Android asks again for each folder

Android shows its own folder permission screen. If it goes wrong:

  • No access given: Try again or Skip the folder.
  • A folder inside it was chosen: Choose all to fix, or Keep the smaller choice.
  • A different folder was chosen: try again or skip.

Nothing outside your chosen folders is scanned or changed.

Choose your Backup Plan

What to do with the photos and videos already on your phone. No plan removes anything.

  • 1. Back up everything not already in the Cloud. Nothing on the phone changes. Selected when you arrive.
  • 2. Back up, then optimise every file on the phone. The most space saved.
  • 3. Back up, then optimise only the files this backup sent.
  • 4. Check the Cloud but send nothing. You choose each album's mode afterwards on the Albums tab.

Good to know

This first backup is one-shot and runs regardless of mode. Afterwards every album is Off, which is correct: from here on you choose each album's mode yourself on the Albums tab. See “My albums say Off after the first backup”.

Optimisation settings during setup

Only for plans 2 and 3.

  • Optimise photos and Optimise video: on or off.
  • Video compression level: High (480p, smallest), Medium (720p) or Low (1080p).
  • Each shows an estimated saving, with a Total estimated savings line. Real results vary.
Ready to Back Up

Shows how much will be backed up and, if optimising, how much space you will save.

  • Right now: starts straight away.
  • Delay: 1h, 2h, 4h, 8h, 12h or 24h.

Good to know

  • A delayed backup starts only while the phone is plugged in, and may start a little late.
  • The app stays on the progress screen until the first backup is finished.
Backup progress

Waiting to start

A countdown runs until the backup starts, even with the app closed, as long as the phone is plugged in. SYNC NOW starts it straight away.

Step 1: Checking your Cloud

Every file is compared with what your Cloud already holds, by name and size, with a running count. Nothing is sent. Usually a minute or two.

Step 2: Uploading

The ring shows overall progress. Below it: the Cloud being sent to and its count. Other Clouds waiting show as Pending.

Step 3: Optimising

Optimising photos, then Optimising video, if your plan includes them.

Buttons

  • Close: closes the app; the backup carries on.
  • Finish: appears when everything is done, with a summary of what was checked, already in the Cloud, and sent.
  • Cancel: asks Stop the backup? Files already sent stay sent; nothing is deleted.
Setup and Settings are separate

Setup and Settings keep their own answers. Setup never reads from Settings, and Settings never reads from setup. Setup's folder list starts empty even if Settings already lists folders, and setup's answers do not appear in Settings.

Setup never sets an album's mode. Only you do, on the Albums tab.

The Albums tab

Where you choose each album's mode and run backups.

How the Albums tab is laid out
  • Green header: mode buttons, totals, and the backup controls.
  • Status line: shown while something is running or just finished.
  • Album list: one card per album, A to Z. Two columns on a wide screen.

Each time you open the tab, it looks at the phone and asks OneDrive again (Rescan reads Checking...). Other Clouds are asked about a file just before it is optimised or removed.

Looking, filtering and scrolling never change a file. Only choosing a mode does.

New albums

When a new album appears, a pop-up says 1 new Album is waiting for you to choose a mode.

  • Show new Albums: lists only the new ones. Show all Albums brings the rest back.
  • Dismiss: closes the message.

New albums carry a New tag and always start at Off. A new album can never start as Archive.

All Albums and the four mode buttons
  • Tap Backup, Sync, Archive or Off to show only the albums in that mode.
  • Tap All Albums, or the same button again, to show them all.

Filtering only changes what you see. To change a mode, use the button on the album's card. See “The four modes”.

Album Mode Count

Album Mode Count: the total for each mode. Shown with All Albums selected. Albums under Off are the ones you have not decided about.

Everything here is backed up

Shown when every album in view has files and none are waiting to be sent. It comes from the app's own record; the Cloud's own answer is the last line of each album card.

Optimised and Saved

With Sync selected: how many files in Sync albums have been optimised, and the space saved.

The originals stay in the Cloud. Restore brings them back. See “How optimising works”.

Files archived and Scheduled to leave this phone

With Archive selected:

  • N files archived · X in your Cloud: files that have left the phone, and the space their copies take in the Cloud.
  • N Scheduled to leave this phone: files still on the phone in Archive albums, not counting files you chose to keep. Nothing left to archive when there are none.

Nothing is removed here. Removal happens on the Archive tab. See “How Archive works, step by step”.

Sync now, Rescan, Pause, Resume and Stop

When nothing is running

  • Sync now: backs up now. If an Optimise switch in Settings is on with its Mode set to Manual, it then optimises too (see “Mode: Automatic or Manual”). Greyed out when there is nothing to send or optimise.
  • Rescan: looks at the phone and asks OneDrive again.

While a backup runs

  • Progress shows as Syncing with a percentage (by data, not file count).
  • Pause: holds all backups until Resume.
  • Stop: ends this run. Automatic backups carry on.

Good to know

  • Sync now does not wait for the charger, but still follows your Wi-Fi setting. See “Use mobile data”.
  • It backs up every album set to Backup, Sync or Archive, but only ever optimises files in Sync albums.
The status line under the card
  • While uploading: the file count, the file being sent, and its progress.
  • While preparing: Scanning... or No permission to read media.
  • After a run: a summary of what applies: uploaded, already in the Cloud, no longer on this phone, failed, waiting on the Cloud (tried again later), still to go, or stopped: with the reason.
The Albums Tab

Header

  • Tap Backup, Sync, Archive or Off to show only the albums in that mode. Tap All Albums to show them all again.
  • The line under the buttons gives the total for each mode.

Album cards

  • Name, file count and size of the album on your phone.
  • Second line (only when needed): how many files are optimised, kept at full size, pending or failed.
  • Cloud line: verified in OneDrive means OneDrive confirmed the files at the right size. It is checked each time you open the tab. Other Clouds show sent to that Cloud.
  • Mode button (right side): tap to change the album's mode. Archive asks you to confirm first. If the album's Cloud cannot do that mode, the card says so.
  • Tap the card to see the album's files. See “An album's file list”.
An album's file list

Opens when you tap an album card.

  • Header: back arrow, album name, mode and file count, Backs up to (the Cloud and folder new files go to, plus any other Cloud already holding some), the counts (“File marks and counts in an album”), Sort by (“Sorting an album's files”) and Keep at full size (“Keep at full size”).
  • Files: one card per file with its size, date and marks. An optimised file shows its smaller size on the phone.
  • Camera folder (if chosen in Settings): extra optimise controls. See “Optimise older photos and videos in your Camera folder”.

No thumbnails or previews. Use your gallery app to look at photos.

File marks and counts in an album
  • ✓ backed up: in the Cloud, full size on the phone.
  • ✓ backed up · optimised: in the Cloud; the phone has a smaller copy.
  • ⟳ pending: waiting to be sent.
  • ✗ failed: could not be sent after several tries.

Retry failed

Retry puts failed files back in the queue and starts a backup. It removes nothing.

Sorting an album's files
  • Name: A to Z.
  • Date: newest first. A restored file has the date it was restored.
  • Status: failed, then pending, then optimised, then backed up.

The list opens in name order each time. Sorting changes nothing about the files.

Keep at full size

A checkbox beside files that Restore brought back. While selected, GallerySync leaves that file alone:

  • In a Sync album, it is not optimised.
  • In an Archive album, it is not removed.
  • In Backup or Off, nothing changes, but the choice is remembered.

Restore selects it automatically. Deselect it to let the file follow its album's mode again.

Optimise older photos and videos in your Camera folder

Only the Camera folder you chose in Settings under Camera Sync (“Camera Sync (Settings)”) has these controls.

Selecting files

  • Select Photos/Videos older than: 1 day to 1 year, or All.
  • Photos and Videos: which kinds to select.
  • Swipe a file right to select, left to deselect. The card shows how many are selected and the estimated saving.

Buttons

  • Sync now: backs up anything waiting in the folder, then optimises the selected files only.
  • Rescan: checks the Cloud again.

Good to know

  • Only files OneDrive has confirmed at full size can be selected.
  • Nothing is optimised until you press Sync now. New photos stay as they are.
  • The Camera folder has no Sync mode, and the Optimise switches in Settings do not affect it.
  • Leaving with changed choices asks whether to make them your defaults.
Selecting files in your Camera folder

Shows how many files are selected and the estimated space saved, or Nothing selected.

  • Photos, Videos and the age select every match.
  • Swipe right to select, left to deselect.
  • Sync now optimises only the selected files.

A greyed file cannot be selected: it is not yet confirmed in OneDrive, or is already optimised. See “Optimise older photos and videos in your Camera folder”.

Duplicate album names detected

A single folder can end up recorded under two spellings that differ only in capital letters. GallerySync spots this, merges them into one album, and sets its mode to Off so you can choose fresh. Dismiss closes the card.

This is the only time the app sets a mode, and it can only set Off.

Archive this album?

Shown when you choose Archive:

  • Archive checks all files are in the Cloud.
  • Archived files move to your phone's Trash/Recycle Bin.
  • Empty the bin to free the space.

Archive confirms; Cancel changes nothing.

Good to know

You confirm once. Files added to the album later are covered too, until the album is empty. Android asks once per batch of up to 2,000 files. See “Android's own confirmation”.

The Restore tab

Brings photos and videos back from your Cloud. It only reads from the Cloud; nothing there is changed.

What Restore brings back
  • To restore: an optimised file on the phone. Restoring puts the full-size original back in its place.
  • To download: a file no longer on the phone. Downloading puts it back in its album.

Restored files get Keep at full size, so they are not optimised or archived again straight away. See “Keep at full size”.

Which Clouds

  • OneDrive: every photo and video in your backup folders, whoever put them there.
  • Dropbox, Google Drive, pCloud, Backblaze B2, IDrive e2: files GallerySync sent from this phone.
  • Google Photos: cannot be restored from.

Where files go

Back into the folder they came from. Files loose at the top of DCIM, Pictures or Movies go back into that folder. If a folder cannot be written, files go to a folder in DCIM named after the album.

Safe to try

A file is replaced only after the full download arrives and its size checks out. If anything fails, the phone's file is left as it was.

Albums to Restore and Files in this album
  • Album list: Albums to Restore, with how many albums have something to bring back.
  • Inside an album: back arrow, album name, and Files in this album with the count and what you have selected.

A dash means the list is still loading. Checking your Cloud for more... means OneDrive is being read. A red message means a Cloud folder could not be reached.

The OneDrive list is remembered, and read again after ten minutes or when you press Refresh.

The message under the number
  • Swipe right to select / left to deselect. Tap to open. on the album list.
  • Swipe right to select / left to deselect → Then press Restore. inside an album.
  • Nothing in your Cloud is missing from this phone, so there is nothing to bring back. when the list is empty.
  • After a restore, how many files came back and how many were left unchanged.
N selected and how much to recover

The files selected across all albums, and the extra space they will take on your phone. Make sure you have that space free.

Refresh, Select all and Clear
  • Refresh (album list): reads the list again, including OneDrive.
  • Select all (inside an album): selects every file in it.
  • Clear: removes every selection.

Greyed out while a restore is running.

The album list

Each album card shows:

  • How many files can come back, and the space they need.
  • How many are to restore and to download.
  • How many are already on this phone (greyed inside; see “Why are some files greyed out?”).
  • How many are selected here, or a check mark when the whole album is selected.

Tap to open. Swipe right to select the whole album, left to deselect.

The file list inside an album

Swipe right (or tap) to select, left to deselect. Each file shows one of:

  • now · full size: an optimised copy, showing its smaller file size on the phone and the full file size in the Cloud.
  • Available for download: not on the phone.
  • Already on this phone: greyed; nothing to do.

While working: Working... with a percentage. Then Restored to full size, Back on this phone, or Could not restore, your file is unchanged with the reason.

Why are some files greyed out?

They are already on the phone at full size (same album, name and size), so there is nothing to restore. They are shown so the album matches your Cloud.

A file with the same name but a different size is not offered: it may be an edit, and Restore never overwrites an edit.

Restore and Stop restoring
  • Restore: brings back every selected file, one at a time. Appears once something is selected.
  • Stop restoring: stops the batch. Files already restored stay restored.

A progress bar shows how many are restored. Needs an internet connection and enough free space.

A photo or video you edited

If you edited an optimised copy and saved over it, restoring would replace your edit, so the app asks: This photo has been edited since it was backed up. Overwrite it with the original?

  • Keep my edits: leaves the file as it is.
  • Overwrite: puts the original back; your edit is replaced.

Good to know

Most editors save a new file, which is never affected. An edited file is backed up as a new file with edited and the date in its name; the original in your Cloud is never replaced.

The Archive tab

The only place files leave your phone. Only albums you set to Archive, checked against your Cloud first, and only after your tap.

How Archive works, step by step

Archive needs Android 11 or newer.

  1. Set an album to Archive on the Albums tab and confirm. See “Archive this album?”.
  2. Press Check these files. Every file is checked against its Cloud. Files not there yet are sent first.
  3. See the result: a check mark or red cross on each file, and how much space will be freed.
  4. Say Yes. Android asks to move the confirmed files to the phone's trash. See “Android's own confirmation”.
  5. Empty the bin when you are ready. The space returns only then.

What "safely" means

The Cloud must confirm, right then, that it holds the file at the same size. If the Cloud cannot be asked, nothing is removed. For an optimised photo, the original's size is checked.

Which Clouds

OneDrive, Google Drive, Dropbox, pCloud, IDrive e2 and Backblaze B2. Not Google Photos.

Good to know

  • Archive needs you present: Android requires a tap. See “Files ready to Archive (the leaving reminder)”.
  • Files added to an Archive album later are covered too.
  • When the last file leaves, the album leaves the list and its mode is forgotten. If it comes back, it starts at Off.
Files to Archive

Files to Archive, with the number of files that will be archived: in every Archive album on the album list, or in the album you opened. Files you kept on the phone are not counted.

Below it: your Archive albums, and a reminder that archived files can be brought back on the Restore tab.

The Archive albums

One card per Archive album: how many files are waiting and their size, plus any kept, held back by the age filter, confirmed, or not confirmed.

  • On the album list, the button reads Check all albums and checks every album.
  • Tap an album to open it; Check these files then checks only that album.

Choosing an album removes nothing and does not change any mode.

Check these files, and what it reports
  • Check these files (or Check all albums): starts the check.
  • Checking with your Cloud... while the Cloud is asked.
  • Batch progress while files are being removed.
  • How many files were removed and the space freed, or Nothing was removed.

OneDrive is checked by listing each album's folder in OneDrive (name and size). Dropbox, Google Drive, pCloud, Backblaze B2 and IDrive e2 are asked about each file.

"Freeing" means after you empty the bin.

Only show files older than…

Limits this check to files at least that old: 1 hour to 1 year, or All. Newer files are greyed and left for a later check.

It starts at your default from Settings. Changing it here lasts for this visit only.

When there is nothing to archive
  • No album is set to Archive: set one on the Albums tab.
  • A zero: everything in your Archive albums has already left the phone.
  • This version of Android has no media trash: Archive needs Android 11 or newer.
The file list and its marks

One card per file in your Archive albums.

Keeping a file on the phone

Use it for a file you want to keep on the phone while the rest of the album is archived. Swipe left to keep it: it greys out and reads Not archiving, and is remembered. Swipe right to include it again. A file greyed as too recent for your filter is held back by the age filter.

Marks

  • Spinner: being checked, sent or removed.
  • Green check mark: confirmed in your Cloud, or removed.
  • Red cross: not confirmed; it stays on the phone.

Messages

Backing up..., Moving to Trash/Recycle Bin..., Removed from this phone., or in red why a file stays: Could not check your Cloud, Not in your Cloud, or In your Cloud but the wrong size.

The question: All files validated, or some validated

After the check:

  • All files validated: every file is confirmed.
  • N files validated: only those are confirmed; the rest stay on the phone.
  • Nothing can be archived: none were confirmed. Continue closes the message.

Yes asks Android to move the confirmed files to the bin. No removes nothing. A large album may need several Android confirmations (2,000 files each).

Android's own confirmation

Android asks you to allow moving the files to the trash. Its wording varies by phone.

  • Android allows 2,000 files per request, so a large album is done in batches.
  • If you say no, nothing is removed.
Files ready to Archive (the leaving reminder)

Appears if you press Back to leave while files are confirmed and waiting to be archived.

  • Archive now: opens the Archive tab.
  • Leave: closes the app. Nothing is removed.

Counts OneDrive files only: only OneDrive copies are confirmed ahead of time. Other Clouds are checked when you press Check these files. The reminder does not appear if you press Home or swipe the app away.

The Settings tab

One scrolling page in green bands: General, Backup, Albums, Sync, Camera Sync, Restore, Archive and Help & Feedback. Each band has a (?).

How the Settings tab is laid out
  • Changes take effect straight away. There is no Save button.
  • Nothing here removes a file from your phone. Only Archive does that.
  • Settings and first-time setup are separate. See “Setup and Settings are separate”.
General

The How To Guide, Appearance and Use mobile data. Language is the last line on the page.

The How To Guide card

Opens this guide. Read more in the How To Guide in any (?) opens it at that topic. Needs an internet connection; if it will not load, use Open in browser.

Language

The language you chose on the Welcome screen. Tap it to change. The How To Guide follows this choice; the app's screens are in English for now.

Appearance
  • System (default): follows your phone's light or dark setting.
  • Light or Dark: always that look.

The guide and policy pages follow this setting too.

Use mobile data
  • Off (default): Wi-Fi only.
  • On: Syncs on Wi-Fi and mobile data.

Covers automatic backups and Sync now. Leave it off unless your data plan is unlimited.

Backup
  • Clouds: connect or sign out of each Cloud. See “Your Clouds and Sign out”.
  • Where each folder goes: which Cloud each folder sends to. See “Where each folder goes”.

One Cloud is marked main (free): the first Cloud you selected. It is always free. Other Clouds need Pro: free for 30 days (Start 30-day free trial), then a one-time purchase (Unlock Pro). Nothing is charged automatically.

Your Clouds and Sign out

Each Cloud shows its account (or Not connected) with Sign out, Connect or Enter keys.

Backup folder

Under each connected Cloud (except Google Photos): the folder its backups go to, with Change. See “Where new backups go (the Change dialog)”.

Sign out

A warning first: backups to that Cloud stop, nothing is deleted. If that Cloud holds files that are not full size on the phone (optimised or archived), it asks:

  • Restore them to the phone first: brings them all back, then signs out.
  • Leave them there: signs out.
  • Cancel: stays signed in.

Folders stay paired with that Cloud and wait until you sign in again. To send them elsewhere, change Where each folder goes.

Where each folder goes

Each top-level folder (DCIM, Pictures, Movies), the Cloud it goes to, and where in that Cloud.

  • Tap the Cloud to change it. It can only be changed with more than one Cloud and Pro or the trial.
  • Only new files follow a change. Files already sent stay where they are.
  • A folder paired with an extra Cloud without Pro sends nothing, and says so.
Where new backups go (the Change dialog)

Opened by Change beside a Cloud's Backup folder, in Settings or on its card during setup.

  • Type the folder path, or for OneDrive use Browse....
  • Reset to default: back to Samsung Gallery/DCIM (OneDrive) or GallerySync (other Clouds).
  • Use this folder saves; Cancel changes nothing.

Only new files go to the new folder. Files already backed up stay where they are. OneDrive keeps checking earlier folders, so nothing is sent twice.

Choose a folder (the OneDrive picker)

Opened by Browse... for OneDrive. Lists your OneDrive folders: tap to open, Up one folder to go back, Use this folder to choose, New folder to create one.

Albums

Which folders GallerySync watches, and what happens to Cloud copies when you delete from the phone. New albums always start at Off.

Folders to back up

The folders GallerySync may look in.

  • Add a folder: opens Android's folder picker.
  • Remove: select folders, press Remove, and confirm.

Nothing outside these folders is scanned or changed. Removing a folder loses nothing: add it back and everything returns.

Stop watching this folder?

Remove stops watching the selected folders; Cancel changes nothing.

Nothing already backed up is lost. Adding the folder back restores its albums and history, with nothing sent twice.

When you delete a photo or video from this phone
  • Leave the Cloud copy (default): nothing is ever removed from your Cloud.
  • Ask me about the Cloud copy: when files leave your phone, a window asks what to do with their Cloud copies. If notifications are allowed, you are also told shortly after deleting. Nothing is removed without your say-so. See “Files deleted from your phone (the window that opens with the app)”.

OneDrive only for now. Copies in other Clouds are never removed.

Files deleted from your phone (the window that opens with the app)

Opens before the Albums tab when files have left your phone, under Ask. Nothing is selected to start with.

Window 1: a copy is in OneDrive

Swipe right (or tap) to select files whose OneDrive copy should go.

  • Remove N from OneDrive: asks you to confirm, then moves those copies to the OneDrive recycle bin. Unselected files stay in OneDrive. See “Remove files from OneDrive? (the confirmation)”.
  • Keep all in OneDrive.
  • Decide later.

Window 2: no copy found

These files are still in your phone's trash.

  • Back up N to OneDrive: sends the selected files from the trash. Nothing is deleted.
  • Leave all in the trash.
  • Decide later.

Good to know

  • Undecided files stay on the list until you decide.
  • Not listed: files Archive removed, photos edited in place, and files deleted outright with no Cloud copy.
  • If more than half of your backed-up files seem to vanish at once, nothing is offered; it is treated as a faulty scan rather than real deletions.
  • Back does the same as Decide later.
Remove files from OneDrive? (the confirmation)

Shows how many files and their size. They go to the OneDrive recycle bin, which GallerySync never empties.

Remove from OneDrive goes ahead; Cancel decides nothing. Any file that has come back to the phone is left alone.

Sync

How photos and videos in Sync albums are optimised. Files change only after the Cloud has verified them. Works with OneDrive, Google Drive, Dropbox, pCloud, IDrive e2 and Backblaze B2.

Optimise photos

Off by default. When on, photos in Sync albums are replaced with smaller copies: about 2048 pixels on the long edge, roughly a tenth of the size. They stay in your gallery with a small cloud badge. Originals stay in the Cloud.

Photos already small enough, and files set to Keep at full size, are left alone. Mode sets when it runs. See “Mode: Automatic or Manual”.

Optimise video

Off by default. When on, shows Mode, Older than and Compression.

Videos in Sync albums are re-encoded smaller. Nothing is ever cut. Originals stay in the Cloud.

Which videos

In a Sync album, verified in the Cloud, older than your setting, in a folder you gave access to, and not already optimised.

When

  • Automatic: after backups, only while charging.
  • Manual: when you press Sync now.
Mode: Automatic or Manual
  • Automatic (default): files in Sync albums are optimised once the Cloud confirms them. Video waits for the charger.
  • Manual: nothing happens until you press Sync now on the Albums tab.

Photos outside the folders you gave access to need Android's confirmation, so they wait until you open the app or press Sync now.

Older than (video)

How old a video must be before it is optimised: Straight away, 1 hour, 12 hours, 1 day or 1 week. Backup is not delayed.

Straight away includes clips shot today; editing one starts from the smaller copy until you restore it.

Compression (video)
  • High compression, 480p: smallest files, about 85% saved.
  • Medium compression, 720p: about 75% saved.
  • Low compression, 1080p: about 50% saved.

Typical figures; results vary.

After you make it stronger

The app asks Re-optimise existing videos? Yes lets videos that were too small to shrink before be tried again. No leaves them. Already optimised videos are not touched.

Restore (Settings)

One switch for the Restore tab: Show empty folders.

Show empty folders

Off by default. When on, the Restore tab lists every OneDrive folder, including ones with nothing to bring back.

Camera Sync (Settings)

Special settings for Camera, off by default. When on:

  • Camera folder: the folder your camera saves to. Choose it from the list, or Other….
  • Select Photos/Videos older than, Photos, Videos: defaults for that folder's optimise controls (“Optimise older photos and videos in your Camera folder”).
  • Video compression: for videos optimised there.

The Camera folder has no Sync mode, and nothing is optimised until you press Sync now in it. The Optimise switches above do not affect it.

Archive (Settings)
  • Only show files older than: where the Archive tab's filter starts. See “Only show files older than (Settings)”.
  • Notify when files are ready to archive: off by default. See “Notify when files are ready to archive”.
Only show files older than (Settings)

Where the Archive tab's age filter starts: 1 hour, 1 day, 1 week, 1 month, 1 year or All (default). Changing it on the Archive tab lasts for that visit only. See “Only show files older than…”.

Notify when files are ready to archive

Off by default. When on, you are notified once per new batch of files ready to archive. OneDrive files only.

The Albums tab and the leaving reminder show this too, so you are never relying on notifications alone. If notifications are blocked, the switch says so.

Help & Feedback, and the link cards at the bottom

Help & Feedback

  • Rate us on Play Store: opens the GallerySync listing.
  • Bug Report: where to write, and Copy details for your app version, phone model and Android version.

At the bottom

  • Privacy Policy.
  • Delete Account Info: how to sign out, remove the app's access and clear its data.
  • Contact Info: the address, with Copy address.

Pages load from the internet. If one will not load, use Open in browser.

How it works, in plain English

The ideas behind the buttons.

The four modes

Each album has one mode, set with the button on its card.

  • Off: this album is not looked after: nothing is sent or changed. Every album starts here.
  • Backup: copies to your Cloud; the phone is never touched.
  • Sync: backs up, then optimises if optimising is on in Settings.
  • Archive: backs up, verifies, then moves the files to the phone's trash after your tap. The only mode that removes files.

Which Clouds

Backup works with every Cloud. Sync and Archive need OneDrive, Google Drive, Dropbox, pCloud, IDrive e2 or Backblaze B2, not Google Photos.

Camera folder

If you set a Camera folder in Settings, it offers Off, Backup and Archive, with its own optimise controls instead of Sync. See “Optimise older photos and videos in your Camera folder”.

Which to pick

  • Keep as is, but protected: Backup.
  • Save space but keep viewing: Sync.
  • Old albums you want off the phone: Archive.
  • Unsure: Off or Backup.

Good to know

  • Only you set modes. The one exception is merging duplicate albums, which sets Off. See “Duplicate album names detected”.
  • Switching to Archive asks you to confirm. Switching away stops further removals.
How verification works

Before anything is optimised or removed, the Cloud is asked, right then, whether it holds a good copy.

The test

  • OneDrive: lists the album folder; the file must have the same name and size.
  • Dropbox, Google Drive, pCloud, Backblaze B2, IDrive e2: asked about the exact file; it must be present, not in its bin, at the same size. For an optimised photo, the original's size.

When

  • At the start of the first backup, so only missing files are sent.
  • Each time you open the Albums tab or press Rescan (OneDrive).
  • When you check files on the Archive tab, and again just before removal.
  • Just before a file is optimised.

Three answers

  • Verified: the Cloud has it.
  • Not there, or wrong size: the file stays on the phone.
  • Could not check: treated as unknown. Nothing is removed or optimised.

Good to know

A size check cannot catch every kind of damage. Open your Cloud now and then and check a few photos.

How optimising works

Optimising swaps the phone's copy for a smaller one, so the phone stops filling up while everything stays in your gallery.

Photos

Reduced to about 2048 pixels on the long edge, roughly a tenth of the size. Same name, place, date and location, with a small cloud badge.

Video

Re-encoded at 480p (High compression), 720p (Medium) or 1080p (Low). Never cut. Automatic waits for the charger; Manual runs on Sync now.

Rules

  • Only in Sync albums.
  • Only after the Cloud confirms the original at the same size.
  • A file that would not get smaller is left alone.

Getting the original back

Use the Restore tab. Restore before editing if you want full detail.

Where removed files go

Nothing is permanently deleted.

On your phone

Archive moves files to Android's trash for about 30 days:

  • Samsung: Samsung Gallery's Recycle Bin.
  • Other phones: the Files app's Trash.

Files in the bin still take their full space until you empty it.

In your Cloud

Under Ask, copies you choose to remove go to the OneDrive recycle bin. Nothing is ever removed from other Clouds. The app never empties any bin.

When things happen
  • Backing up: shortly after new photos appear, and every six hours. Wi-Fi only unless mobile data is on; not when battery or storage is low. Sync now runs straight away.
  • Optimising photos: Automatic, once the Cloud confirms a file in a Sync album. Manual, on Sync now.
  • Optimising video: Automatic, after backups, while charging. Manual, on Sync now.
  • Deleted files: under Ask, you are notified shortly after deleting a file that has a Cloud copy (not while backups are paused).
  • Archiving: only when you say Yes on the Archive tab.
  • Restoring: only when you press Restore.

Closing the app

Back or Home is fine: work carries on. Swiping the app away from recent apps can stop background work until you open it again.

Where your data lives
  • Photos and videos: go directly between your phone and your own Cloud, encrypted. There are no GallerySync servers.
  • Sign-ins and keys: kept encrypted on your phone. Passwords are typed on the provider's page, never in the app.
  • The app's records and settings: private storage on your phone.
  • Nothing is collected: no analytics, crash reporting or ads.

Details: Privacy Policy and Delete Account Info in Settings.

Why the numbers may differ from your gallery app

GallerySync counts only files on the phone now, in the folders you chose, not in the trash. Your gallery may count cloud-only items or group folders differently. Both are right; they count different things.

Questions and problems

Common questions and what is usually going on.

Sync now is greyed out

There is nothing to send or optimise: everything is already sent, or no album is set to Backup, Sync or Archive. Check the mode totals in the header.

My albums say Off after the first backup

That is correct. The first backup sends everything regardless of mode, and setup never sets modes. Choose a mode for each album on the Albums tab.

An album says Not checked against OneDrive yet

OneDrive has not been asked yet. Wait a moment or press Rescan. Could not reach OneDrive means the connection failed: check you are online and signed in, then Rescan.

Albums on other Clouds show sent to that Cloud instead. See “The Albums Tab”.

The backup stopped because my Cloud is full

stopped: your Cloud is full. Nothing is lost. Free some room or add storage, then press Sync now.

I archived an album but my phone has no more space

Archived files sit in the phone's trash, still taking space. Empty the bin once you are happy they are safe in your Cloud. See “Where removed files go”.

An album has disappeared from my gallery

If it was set to Archive, its files are in the phone's trash. Restore them from the bin, or use the Restore tab. It comes back as a new album set to Off.

A photo looks smaller or lower quality than before

It has been optimised (look for the small cloud badge). The original is in your Cloud: use the Restore tab.

The Restore tab says there is nothing to bring back

Nothing has been optimised or archived, and (for OneDrive) every photo in your backup folders is already on the phone. That is correct.

Backups seem to stop when I close the app

Back or Home is fine. Swiping the app away from recent apps can stop background work: open the app again and it carries on without sending anything twice.

I signed in to a Cloud with the wrong account

Settings → Backup → Sign out beside that Cloud, choose Leave them there, then sign in with the right account. Files already sent stay in the first account. See “Your Clouds and Sign out”.

I signed out of a Cloud and its folders stopped sending

That is expected. The folders wait, safe on your phone, until you sign in again. To send them elsewhere, change Where each folder goes. See “Where each folder goes”.

IDrive e2 or Backblaze B2 says my keys were rejected

Usually a typo. Check the endpoint (without https://), region, bucket and both keys; tap Show on the secret. Watch O vs zero, I vs l, J vs j. Pasting avoids this. See “Connecting Backblaze B2: the keys and where to find them” and “Connecting IDrive e2: the keys and where to find them”.

Archive says it could not check my Cloud

The Cloud did not answer, so nothing was removed. Check you are online and signed in, then press Check these files again.

Restore says to reconnect that Cloud

The Cloud refused to let the file be read. Sign in again in Settings. For Dropbox, allow reading files; for IDrive e2 and Backblaze B2, use a key that can read the bucket. Your phone's file was not changed.

GallerySync cannot see my photos

A message at the top of the Albums tab means GallerySync does not have full access to your photos:

  • GallerySync needs access to your photos: no access was given, or it was taken away.
  • Only some photos are shared: access was limited with Select photos, so backups are incomplete.

Press Grant access and choose Allow all. If no prompt appears: phone Settings → Apps → GallerySync → Permissions → Photos and videos.

Contact, privacy and deleting your data

At the bottom of Settings:

  • Contact Info: the address, with a copy button.
  • Privacy Policy: your files go only to your own Cloud; nothing is collected.
  • Delete Account Info: how to sign out, remove access and clear data. Your Cloud files stay.

To report a problem, use Bug Report just above them.
